submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the head noun (or the modal/auxiliary right after it) of the SUBJECT of an object-extracted relative clause or wh-question in abstract expository, technical, business or patent prose, i.e. at the point where a subject has been read and the verb whose object is the already-mentioned filler is due ("the advantages that renewable energy [[sources]] offer", "the effects that environmental [[conditions]] have", "calm that only nature [[can]] provide", "what does this [[all]] mean", "the trust Sentosa [[Care]] has in us"); it is strongest when both the extracted head noun and the subject are abstract (benefits/impact/role + policies/conditions/sources), weak (<0.3 of max) for the same nouns in an 'of'-phrase, and near zero in concrete everyday narrative ("the toys that my little brother left", "the book that my sister wrote") and on ordinary simple sentences; there is no first-token or positional floor. Secondary leftovers: 'not' in 'which/what it does not', the 't' of "doesn't" before a main verb, the stock phrase "The present invention", and end-of-identifier tokens of class/type names in code ("InputMethodSettings[[Interface]] {", "VpnSites[[Client]] struct").
